title: budgeted-latency-econ-optimizer-prefill-profiles
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce Budgeted Latency Econ Optimizer: new service that auto-synthesizes prefill and batch defaults, selects quantization profiles by tenant cost/latency budget, and exposes a dry-run simulator CLI. Backwards compatible; gated behind runtime feature flag.
description: Motivation: Customers want predictable latency while minimizing per-token costs. Current defaults are one-size-fits-all; this PR introduces a Budgeted Latency Economic Optimizer that synthesizes tenant-aware prefill/batching defaults, recommends quantization profiles, and emits unit-econ estimates so platform teams can set budgets and observe expected cost/latency tradeoffs. Design: 1) econ/optimizer core: lightweight planner that consumes recent workload histograms, SLO target (p99 latency budget or tail), and per-tenant cost weights to propose: batch shape, prefill thresholds, KV cache TTL hints, and quantization profile candidate list. 2) unit-econ calculator: simulates expected tokens/costs for a proposed policy and reports estimated cost-per-request and cost-per-token deltas. 3) simulator CLI (cli/econ-sim) to run deterministic dry-runs from replayed traces for safety. 4) runtime integration: conservative canary rollout flag in request-router; metrics tag prefills with econ.plan_id and reported expected_cost/expected_latency for trace-level debugging. 5) Telemetry: new metrics (econ.plan.apply_rate, econ.sim.delta_cost, econ.qprofile.selection_count). Safety: always include fallback to tenant-defaults; quantization proposals include quality regression guard that requires eval suite pass. Checklist: - [x] core planner implementation - [x] unit-econ simulator and CLI - [x] runtime integration and safe feature flag - [x] telemetry and dashboards stub - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs RFC and console panel. Backwards compatibility: config is off by default and only applied to tenants with explicit opt-in or during canary. See linked Linear ENG-2145 for rollout plan and acceptance criteria.

review_comments: Diego Ramirez (2026-02-22): Nice direction. Can you clarify how the planner weights latency vs unit-cost? Suggest exposing a tunable weight and defaulting to a conservative latency-first profile.
Asha Patel (2026-02-22): Reply: planner accepts an explicit weight param (tenant.policy.latency_vs_cost) and defaults to 0.8 latency priority. Added docs note and tests to cover extremes.
Lin Tang (2026-02-24): Concern: qprofile selection could introduce quality regressions. Please wire the eval check and block applying profiles that reduce eval score beyond configured delta.
Asha Patel (2026-02-24): Reply: Added pkg/eval/qprofile_guard.go and integrated it into the apply path; CLI sim runs the eval suite by default in dry-run mode.
Megan O'Connor (2026-02-25): Minor: telemetry names should be namespaced econ.* and match the dashboard. Also caught a flaky test in integration - reworked timing to be stable.
Asha Patel (2026-02-25): Reply: Renamed metrics and updated dashboard stubs. Re-ran flaky integration tests and added a 50ms jitter guard to avoid timing races.
